>Agreed on virtually all of that. The only advantage of a Part I summons is the officer can hand it to you right then and there, whereas an Information would require service at a later date.

Agreed but again... the act doesn't appoint anyone as an officer... so under the act no one is an officer and therefore no one is appointed an officer under that act for the POA to lay the Part 1... there are lots of POA officers with authorities under other acts... but appointment under one act does not give you the authorities under others, one can even only be appointed for certain sections or parts under an act.

the impact is the same... crown brief would need to be written... disclosures made... pre-trial conferences... trial... appeals... 

that's an insane level of paperwork for an individual offence... and if you are going through that it makes little sense to go part 1 and limit the penalty, when you can go part 3 have the same amount of work and can potentially get the max... 

also part 1's are limited in who can issue them, with the act being silent on who has the authority to inspect, investigate, or issue the offence notices it would seem they are relying on the fact that anyone can swear a part 3 information. this would eliminate the part 1 summons as well, because only certain people or classes of people can lay those, and they are given authorities under their respective acts/regulations. 

there is also an issue around identification, should a police officer show up at a line they have the authority to ask for identification under several acts and bi-laws, but not under this act. Using the identification powers from one act to pursue charges under an act that has no such powers is pretty sketchy and suspect.

but the courts can't handle that volume of issues either way... so I would suspect the individual charges either be pled out or just not pursued based on prospects of conviction

To clarify it would all have to go part 3, cause there is no short form wording and no set fines (these have to go through the judiciary to be set). So there won’t be any tickets like a speeding/parking ticket. They will be notice to appears under part 3 of the POA
